bib.title: CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2020

read.skipped: References skimmed only; figure images (Fig 1-7) not viewed, only captions and extracted text.

question: Can a single Transformer pre-trained on paired natural language and code (plus unpaired code) give general-purpose representations that improve NL-PL tasks such as code search and documentation generation?
hypothesis: Using both bimodal NL-PL pairs and unimodal code, via MLM plus replaced token detection, gives better NL-PL representations than text-only (RoBERTa) or code-only pre-training.
contributions: CodeBERT is the first large NL-PL pre-trained model for multiple programming languages.
Empirical results show that CodeBERT is effective in both code search and code-to-text generation tasks.
A dataset, the first to investigate the probing ability of code-based pre-trained models.

method.summary: A RoBERTa-base-sized bidirectional Transformer is pre-trained on CodeSearchNet NL-PL pairs (MLM) and unimodal code/NL (replaced token detection with n-gram generators), one model for six languages. It is then fine-tuned for code search and code-to-NL generation, and probed zero-shot with a cloze-style multiple-choice dataset the authors built.
method.task: Bimodal NL-PL pre-training (MLM + replaced token detection); downstream code search, NL-PL probing, code documentation generation

datasets.name: CodeSearchNet (Husain et al. 2019), pre-training use
datasets.size: 2.1M bimodal datapoints (2,137,293) and 6.4M unimodal codes (6,452,446), six languages
datasets.split: training data only; no access to dev and test data
datasets.source: public open-source non-fork GitHub repositories (Python, Java, JavaScript, PHP, Ruby, Go)
datasets.preprocessing: Filters: each project used by at least one other project; documentation truncated to first paragraph; documentation shorter than three tokens removed; functions shorter than three lines removed; function names containing 'test' removed. Per-language counts in Table 1 (bimodal/unimodal): Go 319,256/726,768; Java 500,754/1,569,889; JavaScript 143,252/1,857,835; PHP 662,907/977,821; Python 458,219/1,156,085; Ruby 52,905/164,048.

datasets.name: CodeSearchNet corpus, code search
datasets.split: official train/dev/test; best dev model evaluated on test
datasets.preprocessing: Balanced positives and negatives; negatives are an equal mix of randomly replaced NL (c, w-hat) and replaced PL (c-hat, w).

datasets.name: NL-PL probing set (built by authors)
datasets.size: PL probing 2,615 datapoints (2 choices); NL probing 856 datapoints (4 choices)
datasets.split: drawn from validation and test sets of CodeSearchNet, unseen in pre-training
datasets.source: automatic selection by keyword from CodeSearchNet pairs
datasets.preprocessing: NL side: docs containing one of max, maximize, min, minimize, less, greater; grouped into 4 candidates (first two merged, middle two merged). PL side: code containing max and min, 2 candidates. An extra PL setting gives only preceding code context.

models.name: CodeBERT
models.architecture: multi-layer bidirectional Transformer, exactly RoBERTa-base architecture
models.init_from: from scratch (INIT=S) or RoBERTa parameters (INIT=R); headline model uses INIT=R
models.tokenizer: NL as WordPiece; code as a sequence of tokens
models.layers: inferred: 12, from 'exactly the same model architecture as RoBERTa-base' (not printed)

other.generators: two bidirectional n-gram language models, one NL and one PL, learned from unimodal data; discarded at fine-tuning

models.name: Pre-train w/ code only (INIT=S / INIT=R)
models.architecture: same as CodeBERT, MLM on code only

other.note: RoBERTa continuously trained with MLM only on codes from CodeSearchNet

models.name: NBOW, CNN, BiRNN, SelfAtt
models.architecture: joint embedding models of NL and PL

other.note: numbers reported by Husain et al. (2019)

training.objective: min over theta of L_MLM + L_RTD (Eq 14). MLM on bimodal data, 15% of tokens of x masked. RTD (Clark et al. 2020) on every position: binary original vs replaced; a token the generator gets right keeps label 'real'. RTD uses both bimodal and unimodal data.
training.hardware: one NVIDIA DGX-2 machine, 16 interconnected NVIDIA Tesla V100 with 32GB memory
training.wall_clock: Training 1,000 batches of data costs 600 minutes with MLM objective, 120 minutes with RTD objective (as printed; 100K steps total time not stated)

other.finetune_code_search: lr 1e-5, batch size 64, max seq length 200, max 8 epochs, Adam; model best on dev used for test; one language-specific model per language; binary classification loss with softmax on [CLS]
other.finetune_summarization_six_languages: decoder is Transformer with 6 layers, 768 hidden, 12 heads; max input length 256, max inference length 64; Adam; lr 5e-5, batch size 64; tune hyperparameters and early stop on dev
other.finetune_csharp: decoder 2-layer GRU with attention; grid search batch size {32, 64}, lr {2e-5, 5e-5}; best on dev reported
other.late_fusion: CodeBERT encodes NL and PL separately, dot-product similarity, softmax contrastive loss over candidates (Eq 15); run only on Ruby and Go

inference.max_tokens: inference max length 64 for six-language code summarization
inference.samples: single run per setting; no seeds or repeats stated
inference.retrieval: code search: rank 999 fixed distractor codes per (c, w) test pair; MRR

metrics.name: MRR (macro-average over six languages, MA-AVG)
metrics.definition: Mean Reciprocal Rank for each test pair (c, w) over a fixed set of 999 distractor codes; differs from the AVG metric of Husain et al., where candidates come from all six languages

metrics.name: Probing accuracy
metrics.definition: correctly predicted instances over all instances; pooled across languages in ALL column

metrics.name: Smoothed BLEU-4
metrics.definition: smoothed BLEU (Lin and Och 2004) for short generated documentation; C# uses the evaluation scripts of Iyer et al. 2016

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, variance or significance test stated. Probing is zero-shot with parameters fixed, using CodeBERT (MLM) because its output layer fits probing.

availability.weights: inferred: via the same GitHub link (the paper says 'All the codes and data are available')
availability.data: CodeSearchNet (public); probing data at the GitHub link

results.setup: CodeSearchNet, pre-trained encoder with 6-layer Transformer decoder
results.quote: brings a gain of 1.3 BLEU score over RoBERTa overall

results.claim: On C# (language unseen in pre-training), CodeBERT (MLM+RTD) improves 2.55 BLEU over RoBERTa but stays below code2seq (23.04), which uses AST paths.

results.quote: achieves 22.36 BLEU score and improves by 2.55

results.claim: Late-fusion (separate encoders, dot product) code search: CodeBERT far above RoBERTa, whose raw encoder is almost useless in this setting.
Pre-training cost: MLM costs 600 minutes per 1,000 batches versus 120 for RTD.
results.quote: Training 1,000 batches of data costs 600 minutes with MLM objective, 120 minutes with RTD objective.

limits: RTD generators are simple n-gram language models, not neural; authors leave bimodal or Transformer generators to future work.
Loss functions mainly target NL-PL understanding, not generation; no generation-based pre-training objective.
No AST input: a CodeBERT trained on a traversed AST gave no generation improvement; code2seq with AST paths beats it on C#.
Single run per setting, no seeds, variance or significance tests stated, so small gaps (e.g. 0.7549 vs 0.7603 MRR) are not testable.
Probing set is small and uneven across languages (Ruby 20 NL items, 38 PL items) and built from only max/min style keywords, so it tests narrow knowledge.
Probing used the MLM-only model, not the MLM+RTD model.
Multilingual fine-tuning for code search was tried but performed worse than language-specific models; the numbers are not given.
Layers, hidden size, heads, vocab, weight decay, dropout and lr schedule are not printed (only 'same as RoBERTa-base').
Late fusion tested on two languages only.

figures.caption: An illustration about the replaced token detection objective. Both NL and code generators are language models, which generate plausible tokens for masked positions based on surrounding contexts. NL-Code discriminator is the targeted pre-trained model, which is trained via detecting plausible alternatives tokens sampled from NL and PL generators.
figures.why: Shows the generator/discriminator pipeline and which parts are discarded at fine-tuning; shows why unimodal code can feed RTD.

figures.caption: Results on natural language code retrieval (init scratch vs RoBERTa; MLM, RTD, MLM+RTD)
figures.why: One ablation grid for objective and initialisation choices.

figures.caption: Case study on python language. Masked tokens in NL and PL are separately applied. Predicted probabilities of RoBERTa and CodeBERT are given.
figures.why: Concrete probing example where RoBERTa picks 'max' with 96% and CodeBERT gets PL right at 99.999%.

figures.caption: An example of the NL-PL pair, where NL is the first paragraph from the documentation of a function.
figures.why: Defines what a bimodal datapoint is.
